newsitem.title: USA: Norfolk sees greater Conrail deal benefits.
newsitem.headline: Norfolk sees greater Conrail deal benefits.

text.p: Norfolk Southern Corp has revised upward its estimates of cost savings and 1999 earnings accretion from the acquisition of portions of Conrail Inc, Chief Financial Officer Henry Wolf said Wednesday.
The company also has cut its estimate of earnings dilution in 1998, he said at a presentation of the company's second quarter earnings.
Operating expense savings should total $86 million in 1998, $327 million in 1999, and $564 million in 2000, Wolf said.
In April the company estimated savings of $71 million in 1998, $236 million in 1999, and $399 million in 2000.
Norfolk Southern still sees earnings dilution of two percent in 1997, but only one-two percent in 1998 as opposed to earlier estimates of three percent.
Earnings accretion is expected to be 14 percent in 1999, Wolf said, as opposed to an April estimate of six percent.
Norfolk Southern and CSX Corp propose to buy Conrail and divide the company between them.
The companies have submitted their plan to the Surface Transportation Board (STB), which has said it will take 350 days to review the proposal.
Earnings accretion from the merger is expected to be 25 percent by the year 2000, as opposed to an April projection of 15 percent, Wolf said.
"That assumes the STB approval comes in early June of 1998, and we are able to affect the synergies beginning July 1, 1998," he said.
Norfolk Southern still expects a 50 percent revenue boost immediately upon completing the merger.
Wolf told analysts at the presentation that the company now plans net capital spending in the period 1998-2000 to $506 million, down from an April projection of $527 million.
The company now anticipates that over $1.5 billion of debt will be retired by the end of the year 2000, compared with an April projection of $1.2 billion.

Wolf also said that although Norfolk Southern does not have a final appraisal for Conrail, it expects little, if any, goodwill to result from the deal because the appraised value of Conrail properties is expected to exceed the purchase price.
